scope_findings.claim: The project is led by an excellent experienced researcher (Dr. Rositsa Cholakova, PhD 2020 summa cum laude, specialist in non-destructive evaluation of drought-stressed plants) undertaking international mobility from Bulgaria (Plovdiv) to Hungary (Budapest, ELTE).

The fellowship is structured as a European Postdoctoral Fellowship (EF) of 24 months duration, involving an intra-EU move from Bulgaria to Hungary, satisfying the EF fellowship form requirement (12–24 months; researcher of any nationality moving within Europe).

A Career Development Plan is prepared jointly by the supervisor (Dr. András Jung, ELTE) and the researcher (Dr. Cholakova), submitted as a project deliverable at the beginning of the action (months 2–3), and reviewed and updated at M12 and M24.

Training integrates digital and AI skills (including responsible use of generative AI in environmental modelling and scientific coding), knowledge valorisation and innovation/entrepreneurship (translating the uncertainty-aware decision-support demonstrator toward user uptake), and research integrity and open-science ethics (FAIR data management, open research software, reproducible validation protocol).

The research project develops an uncertainty-aware, probabilistic, multi-sensor crop water-stress diagnosis and irrigation decision-support framework for tomato (Route B: homogeneous-patch proxy; AquaCrop decision engine calibrated with uncertainty-awareness; water-use efficiency as decision objective).

scope_findings.claim: Validation is conducted using non-destructive physiological measurement (chlorophyll fluorescence, stomatal conductance, canopy/leaf temperature, spectral reflectance) at Hungarian tomato field sites accessed via the associated partner AgroVIR, targeting 90% prediction-interval coverage as the uncertainty calibration criterion, with Route B patch covariation established by a co-located seasonal campaign.

scope_findings.claim: The fellowship delivers a two-way transfer of knowledge (fellow's plant-physiology and non-destructive stress-phenotyping expertise to host's geoinformatics group; host's remote-sensing and multisensor-fusion competences to fellow). Specific researcher career milestone targets are stated: ≥3 peer-reviewed publications (≥2 first-author), ≥120 hours of transferable-skills training, ≥2 methods seminars at the host, co-supervision of ≥1 MSc thesis, and submission of a follow-on national or ERC-track proposal within six months of the fellowship's end.
scope_findings.flag_reason: SR-01 (researcher excellence and international mobility) is the most relevant scope element and partially supports the two-way knowledge-transfer design, but does not enumerate or require the specific quantitative career milestone targets stated (publication counts, training hours, MSc co-supervision, follow-on proposal timeline). These specific targets cannot be confirmed as in-scope against a Tier 2B scope_element_id without risk of drawing on generic MSCA programme knowledge beyond what is extracted in scope_requirements.json. None of the specific targets is excluded by any CC. Flagged pending operator confirmation that these commitments are consistent with the full call requirements (Phase 1 call analysis) or are project-specific choices that do not conflict with any SR/CC.
